summary: This Wikipedia-derived note is a short biography of Hermine Kittel (1879–1948), an Austrian contralto from Vienna. It covers her singing training with Amalie Materna, her operatic debut in Ljubljana in 1897, and her work at the Vienna Hofoper under Gustav Mahler. It also lists her appearances at the Bayreuth and Salzburg festivals and her notable roles.
one_line: Biography of Austrian contralto Hermine Kittel, covering her training, Vienna Hofoper work, and Bayreuth and Salzburg festival appearances.
key_facts: Hermine Kittel was born December 2, 1879 and died April 7, 1948.
Hermine Kittel was an Austrian contralto from Vienna.
Hermine Kittel studied singing with Amalie Materna in Vienna.
Hermine Kittel made her operatic debut in 1897 in Ljubljana.
Hermine Kittel first sang under Gustav Mahler at the Vienna Hofoper (Vienna State Opera).
Hermine Kittel later premiered in a revision of "Ariadne auf Naxos".
Hermine Kittel sang at the Bayreuth Festival in 1902 and 1908.
At the Bayreuth Festival, Hermine Kittel sang Erda in "Der Ring des Nibelungen".
Hermine Kittel also sang at the Salzburg Festival.
At the Salzburg Festival, Hermine Kittel often played Marcellina in "The Marriage of Figaro".
